subject: Aurora Health — SLO qualification: context window tradeoffs & latency impacts
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Kline <sam.k@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Health — initial SLO follow-up and context window notes

Hi Sam — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side with the bits we promised to confirm: 

- Latency target: you mentioned 250ms p50 for synchronous triage flows, and up to 800ms p95 for longer-context summarization flows. Confirm?
- Expected concurrency: ~120 concurrent requests at peak across the triage endpoint; burst to 300 for short windows.
- Typical input size: triage prompts ~400–800 tokens; summarization/patient-history flows occasionally hit 6k–8k input tokens with ~500–1k tokens of generated output.
- Streaming: you want word-by-word streaming for the triage flow; summarization can be chunked streaming or full-response.

Action items we committed to:
1) Attach an SLO matrix mapping your described flows to candidate model variants (LlamaX-13B-Quant / LlamaX-30B-fp16) and rough cost/latency projections.
2) Run a targeted perf simulation based on the 6k+ context scenario to show p95 tail impact and batching behavior.
3) Confirm fallback plan: server-side truncation + chunked summarization vs. raise 2nd-tier model for large-context cases.

I attached the SLO matrix and a quick context-vs-latency plot. Please flag any numbers that don't align with what your infra team expects.

Next steps: if that looks good, can we schedule a 30-min technical touch on Monday to validate the perf sim results with your ops?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurora_SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), context-vs-latency-plot.png (image)
From: Sam Kline <sam.k@aurorahealth.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 17:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health — initial SLO follow-up and context window notes

Jordan — appreciate the clear recap and the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: 250ms p50 is correct for triage. For p95 we can tolerate up to 600ms if streaming starts within ~100ms for perceived interactivity.
- Concurrency: 120 steady, bursts up to 350 are realistic during admission spikes.
- Token sizes: triage tops at ~900 tokens; note that our EHR exports sometimes include dense embedded notes that push summarization to 9k tokens input with up to 2k desired output.
- Streaming: triage must stream incremental tokens to the UI; summarization should at least stream paragraph-by-paragraph.

A couple ask items:
- Can you show a tradeoff table for the latency impact of enabling 9k context vs. using a two-pass chunked approach?
- Any idea on how much additional cost (rough % increase) we should expect to preserve streaming at p95 for those large contexts?

We can do Monday 10am PT for the tech touch if that works. I'll loop in our SRE (procurement@aurorahealth.ai) if we need to discuss capacity planning.

— Sam
Director, Clinical Applications
Aurora Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Kline <sam.k@aurorahealth.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health — initial SLO follow-up and context window notes

Thanks Sam — and appreciated the expanded numbers. Quick notes before the Monday call: 

- Two-pass chunked approach (client sends full context, server pre-splits into ~2.5k token chunks, run chunk-level encodings and then an aggregator pass) generally reduces peak memory and can keep p95 within ~20–40% of small-context p95 at the cost of ~1.4–1.8x compute. That cost range assumes our optimized KV caching is effective for repeated tokens across chunks.
- Full 9k-context on a single inference pass with 30B-class models typically increases per-request latency non-linearly — expect p95 to jump 2x–3x versus a 1k token baseline on identical hardware, and token compute costs to rise similarly.
- Streaming impact: with chunked approach we can start streaming on first chunk within ~120ms for triage-like prompts; aggregator outputs still add tail latency if final synthesis happens server-side.
- Cost guidance: rough estimate +60–110% compute cost to maintain similar p95 streaming behavior for 9k single-pass vs. chunked flow baseline. We'll validate with the perf sim.

I've attached the SLO matrix live link in case you want to edit numbers prior to the call. Proposed agenda for Monday 10am PT:
1) Validate traffic profile (concurrency/burst windows) and token distributions.
2) Review perf sim results (p50/p95/p99) for single-pass vs. chunked.
3) Decide fallback: server truncation + chunked high-fidelity pass vs. 2-model routing (small fast model for triage, large model for long-context).
4) Timeline for a 2-week POC.

If you want Ben to run a quick cost calc for 1M requests/month with your traffic profile, say the word and he'll include that in the call.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Kline <sam.k@aurorahealth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health — initial SLO follow-up and context window notes

Sam — quick note from cost ops: I'll bring a short runbook for estimating unit economics on Monday. Preview:

- Baseline (triage, avg 700 tokens in/out) on LlamaX-13B-Quant: ~$0.003 per request, p95 ~210ms with streaming enabled and small batching.
- Large-context path (9k in / 1.5k out) single-pass on LlamaX-30B-fp16: ballpark $0.014–0.02 per request with p95 in the 700–1,200ms band depending on concurrency and batching.
- Chunked two-pass (3 x 3k chunks + 1 aggregator pass): ~1.6x compute cost vs. single-pass 30B for the same output quality but gives more predictable tail latency and better memory utilization.

I'll prepare a simple spreadsheet that maps your monthly request volume to expected monthly cost under three routing options (always small-fast, always large-single-pass, and hybrid chunked). See you Monday 10am PT (invites on the way).

Ben Carter
Pricing & Solutions, Redwood Inference
